body:
Non-blocking: a stop that lands during `git worktree remove` now leaves a half-removed worktree that the cleaner keeps from then on.

Failing condition: the bound expires while the cleaner's `git worktree remove` is deleting files. The SIGTERM sent to the group here reaches that git, which exits 143 partway through. Before this change only the cleaner was killed, and git ran on to finish. The review subagent reproduced it in a scratch repository: SIGTERM 0.15 s into removing a 20,001-file worktree left it registered with 17,275 files remaining. `scripts/clean-worktrees.py:349-356` then reads it as having uncommitted changes and keeps it on every later run until someone removes it by hand.

Nothing is lost, because the worktree had already passed the finished-work checks. The window is the moment of a removal inside a 180 s bound. Stopping the whole group is the fix the user ruled. Recorded, not blocking.

body:
Question, not a finding (Codex P2, reproduced): the docstring says SIGKILL follows "when the group has not ended", but the code decides from the cleaner alone.

SIGKILL is sent only if `cleaner.communicate()` at line 1384 times out, which happens when the cleaner, or something holding its stdout, outlives the grace. A group member that ignores SIGTERM and does not hold the cleaner's stdout is never sent SIGKILL. The review subagent built one: `communicate` returned at 2.0 s and the child stayed alive. No real member is known to do this: git re-raises after removing its locks, and lsof takes the default action. The comment at lines 167-168 says the same as the docstring. Whether to narrow the wording to "the cleaner" or check the group is an open choice.

body:
Non-blocking test gap: no case exercises the SIGKILL step.

Failing condition: if a later change dropped `signal.SIGKILL` from this tuple, a cleaner that ignores SIGTERM would be left running after the handoff moves on. All 345 cases still pass under that mutation. Both readers checked the escalation by hand, so this head is right; the test just doesn't cover it. A stand-in cleaner that traps SIGTERM and sleeps past the grace would pin it.
